docs.title: Tidewatch
docs.text:
Tidewatch watches your folders and runs tasks when files change. It's a single binary with a small config file, and it's built for the inner loop: rebuild on save, re-run tests, regenerate assets, restart a dev server.

$ tidewatch watch
tidewatch 2.0.0 · loaded tidewatch.yaml (3 tasks)
[styles]  watching src/styles/**/*.scss
[tests]   watching src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py
[server]  watching src/**/*.py
[tests]   src/parser.py changed → pytest -q  ✓ 1.8s

docs.title: Why Tidewatch
docs.text:
• One config, many tasks. Each task has its own paths, ignore rules and command.
  • Debounced by default. Saving 40 files at once triggers one run, not 40.
  • Watch or run once. tidewatch watch for development, tidewatch once for CI.
  • Plugins. Add notifications, restart long-running processes, or filter by git status.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
• Install Tidewatch: get the binary on your machine.
  • Quickstart: your first watch task in two minutes.
  • Configuration: every key in tidewatch.yaml.
  • Coming from v1?: convert your tidewatch.ini.

Breaking changes: see Migrating from v1.

  • Config moved from tidewatch.ini to tidewatch.yaml.
  • tidewatch run split into tidewatch watch and tidewatch once.
  • Debounce is now set in milliseconds with debounce_ms.
  • New plugin system with built-in notify, restart and git-filter plugins.
  • tidewatch init --from tidewatch.ini converts v1 configs.
• ignore patterns in each watch section.
• --once flag for CI.
• First stable release.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: tidewatch <command> [options]

docs.title: Global options
docs.text: Option Description --config <path> Config file to load. Default: ./tidewatch.yaml. --quiet Only print task output and errors. --version Print the version and exit.

docs.title: tidewatch watch
docs.text:
Start watching and run tasks as files change. Runs until interrupted (Ctrl+C).

Option Description --only <name> Run only the named task. Repeatable. --initial Run every task once at startup before watching.

docs.title: tidewatch once
docs.text:
Run every task one time and exit. The exit code is 0 if all tasks succeed, otherwise 1. Use it in CI.

Option Description --only <name> Run only the named task. Repeatable. --parallel Run tasks concurrently instead of in config order.

docs.title: tidewatch init
docs.text: Write a starter tidewatch.yaml in the current directory. Refuses to overwrite an existing file.

docs.title: tidewatch plugins list
docs.text:
List plugins that are installed and which ones the current config loads.

$ tidewatch plugins list
notify      built-in   loaded
restart     built-in   loaded
git-filter  built-in   available

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Tidewatch reads tidewatch.yaml from the current directory. Use --config <path> to load a different file.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
tidewatch.yaml
debounce_ms: 200          # global default

plugins:
  - notify
  - restart

watch:
  - name: styles
    paths: ["src/styles/**/*.scss"]
    run: sass src/styles:dist/css

  - name: tests
    paths: ["src/**/*.py", "tests/**/*.py"]
    ignore: ["**/__pycache__/**", "**/.pytest_cache/**"]
    run: pytest -q
    debounce_ms: 500

  - name: server
    paths: ["src/**/*.py"]
    run: python -m app
    restart: true          # provided by the restart plugin

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Default Description debounce_ms integer 200 Wait this long after the last change before running a task. plugins list of strings [] Plugins to load. See Plugins. watch list of tasks — Required. The tasks to run.

docs.title: Task keys
docs.text:
Key Type Default Description name string — Required. Unique task name, used as the log prefix. paths list of globs — Required. Files that trigger the task. ignore list of globs [] Files to exclude, even if they match paths. run string — Required. Shell command to run. debounce_ms integer global value Per-task override.

Glob syntax

* matches within one directory, ** matches across directories. Paths are relative to the directory containing tidewatch.yaml.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Tidewatch ships as a single static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows.

macOS / Linux (script)HomebrewCargoWindows (Scoop) 
curl -fsSL https://get.tidewatch.dev/install.sh | sh

brew install tidewatch

cargo install tidewatch --version "^2"

scoop install tidewatch

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
$ tidewatch --version
tidewatch 2.0.0

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Platform Minimum version File events backend Linux kernel 4.9 inotify macOS 12 (Monterey) FSEvents Windows 10 ReadDirectoryChangesW

Large repositories on Linux

inotify has a per-user watch limit. If Tidewatch logs too many watches, raise it: sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288.

docs.title: Migrating from v1
docs.text: Tidewatch 2.0 replaces the INI config with YAML and splits tidewatch run into two commands. Most projects can migrate in about five minutes.

docs.title: Summary of breaking changes
docs.text: v1 v2 tidewatch.ini tidewatch.yaml [watch:<name>] section item in the watch: list with name: command = run: delay = (seconds) debounce_ms: (milliseconds) Comma-separated paths YAML list tidewatch run tidewatch watch tidewatch run --once tidewatch once

docs.title: Convert your config
docs.text:
v1: tidewatch.iniv2: tidewatch.yaml 
[watch:tests]
paths = src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py
ignore = **/__pycache__/**
command = pytest -q
delay = 0.5

watch:
  - name: tests
    paths: ["src/**/*.py", "tests/**/*.py"]
    ignore: ["**/__pycache__/**"]
    run: pytest -q
    debounce_ms: 500

Automatic conversion

tidewatch init --from tidewatch.ini reads a v1 config and writes the equivalent tidewatch.yaml. Review the output, then delete the old file.

docs.title: Update scripts and CI
docs.text:
Replace tidewatch run --once with tidewatch once in CI pipelines, and tidewatch run with tidewatch watch in Makefiles and package.json scripts.

Warning

v2 ignores tidewatch.ini. If no tidewatch.yaml exists, Tidewatch exits with error: no tidewatch.yaml found (found tidewatch.ini — see the migration guide).

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plugins add behaviour to tasks. Enable them in the top-level plugins list; some add new task keys.

plugins:
  - notify
  - restart

docs.title: notify
docs.text:
Shows a desktop notification when a task fails, and again when it recovers.

Task key Default Description notify on_failure One of always, on_failure, never.

docs.title: restart
docs.text:
For long-running commands such as dev servers. Instead of starting a second copy, the running process gets SIGTERM and is restarted.

Task key Default Description restart false Enable restart behaviour for this task. stop_timeout_ms 3000 Time to wait before sending SIGKILL.

docs.title: git-filter
docs.text:
Ignores changes to files that git ignores, so build output never re-triggers tasks.

Task key Default Description respect_gitignore true Skip files matched by .gitignore.

Writing your own

Third-party plugins are executables named tidewatch-plugin-<name> on your PATH. They receive events as JSON lines on stdin.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide sets up a task that re-runs your tests every time a Python file changes.

docs.title: 1. Create a config
docs.text:
Run tidewatch init in your project root. It writes a starter tidewatch.yaml:

tidewatch.yaml
watch:
  - name: tests
    paths: ["src/**/*.py", "tests/**/*.py"]
    ignore: ["**/__pycache__/**"]
    run: pytest -q

docs.title: 2. Start watching
docs.text:
$ tidewatch watch
tidewatch 2.0.0 · loaded tidewatch.yaml (1 task)
[tests] watching src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py

Save any matching file and Tidewatch runs pytest -q, streaming its output with a [tests] prefix.

docs.title: 3. Run once in CI
docs.text:
In CI you don't want a long-running watcher. tidewatch once runs every task one time and exits with a non-zero code if any task fails:

$ tidewatch once
[tests] pytest -q  ✓ 2.1s
